short_description: A dataset of ICU admission notes with single-variable counterfactuals (demographics and vital signs) enabling controlled evaluation of medical LLM sensitivity, robustness, and clinical reasoning to meaningful patient data changes.
title: MIMIC-IV-Ext-DeVisE. Counterfactual ICU Admission Notes for Behavioral Evaluation of Medical Language Models
abstract:
MIMIC-IV-Ext-DeVisE contains counterfactual ICU admission notes designed to enable controlled behavioral evaluation of medical large language models (LLMs) to clinically meaningful perturbations in patient data. It was created as part of the DeVisE (Demographics and Vital Signs Evaluation) framework.

The dataset includes 1,001 ICU admission notes derived from MIMIC-IV and 135,861 single-variable counterfactual perturbations: 25,025 for demographics (age, sex, ethnicity) and 110,836 for vital signs (heart rate, blood pressure -systolic and diastolic- , respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and temperature). Vital-sign perturbations are additionally provided in both unstructured and template-based note formats, yielding 246,697 counterfactual records in total across all JSONL files. All other clinical content is preserved, enabling controlled analysis of model sensitivity to clinically meaningful changes.

Two complementary formats are provided: (i) unstructured clinical text derived from discharge summaries and (ii) template-based structured notes containing only variables of interest also derived from discharge summaries. Counterfactual values are sampled from clinically grounded severity ranges to ensure realism and interpretability.

The dataset supports research on robustness, fairness, and clinical reasoning in medical LLMs by enabling controlled, minimally differing input comparisons.

short_description: This version adds DICOM-format mammography images to TN-Mammo alongside the previously available JPEG images. Dataset identifiers have been replaced with UUIDs, while the labels, annotations, and underlying data remain unchanged.
title: TN-Mammo: A Multi-view Mammography Dataset for Breast Density Classification
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common types of cancer among women, leading to a growing and essential need for early and precise detection. A variety of machine learning techniques have been demonstrating great promise in improving diagnostic accuracy integrated with digital mammography, which remains the gold standard screening technique in the detection of early breast cancer. Since the performance of machine learning models generally depends on the quality of training data, it is essential to build a high-quality mammogram dataset. Although there exists a number of public datasets, there are still significant limitations due to both their quality and quantity. We present an extensive Vietnamese mammogram dataset with breast density annotations in an effort to bridge the gap between availability and practical usability. Our mammogram dataset named TNMammo, consists of bilateral craniocaudal (CC) and mediolateral oblique (MLO) views for 676 subjects, each with paired left and right breast views. The breast density and orientation for each case have been independently assessed by two radiologists in a double-blind manner, ensuring consistency and reliability in the annotations. Each case is evaluated based on breast density, categorized into four levels: A, B, C, and D.

short_description: BUT CGM contains 10-day free-living data from 60 healthy active population, including continuous glucose monitoring, electrocardiogram, accelerometry, activity, sleep, food intake, complemented by cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) reference.
title: Brno University of Technology Continuous Glycaemia, ECG, Activity and Food Intake Database (BUT CGM)
abstract: The Brno University of Technology Continuous Glycaemia, ECG, Activity and Food Intake Database (BUT CGM) is a multimodal dataset collected in free-living conditions from a healthy predominantly physically active population. The resource was created to address the lack of publicly available datasets that jointly capture interstitial glucose, high-resolution cardiac electrophysiology, physical activity (sports activity, daily steps), sleep, and detailed dietary intake in everyday life. Data from 60 participants were acquired approximately ten consecutive days using a continuous glucose monitor (CGM), single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG), accelerometry (ACC), entry and daily questionnaires, and detailed food logging, and are complemented by laboratory-based cardiopulmonary exercise testing with ventilatory threshold annotation. The dataset enables research on cardio-metabolic interactions, glycaemic dynamics, and lifestyle–performance relationships under real-world conditions.

short_description: The ER-REASON dataset is a longitudinal collection of 25,174 de-identified clinical notes for 3,437 patients admitted to the emergency room (ER) at a large academic medical center between March 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024.
title: ER-REASON: A Benchmark Dataset for LLM-Based Clinical Reasoning in the Emergency Room
abstract: The ER-Reason dataset is a benchmark designed to evaluate LLM-based clinical reasoning and decision-making in the emergency room (ER), a high-stakes setting where clinicians make rapid, consequential decisions across diverse patient presentations and medical specialties under time pressure. This longitudinal collection of de-identified clinical notes encompasses 3,437 patients admitted to the ER at a large academic medical center between March 1, 2022, and March 31, 2024. ER-Reason contains 25,174 notes spanning discharge summaries, progress notes, history and physical exams, consults, echocardiography reports, imaging notes, and ER provider documentation across 3,984 encounters. The benchmark includes evaluation tasks from key stages of the ER workflow: triage intake, initial assessment, treatment selection, disposition planning, and final diagnosis, each structured to reflect core clinical reasoning processes such as differential diagnosis via rule-out reasoning. We also collected 72 full physician-authored rationales explaining reasoning processes that mimic the teaching process used in residency training, and are typically absent from ER documentation. This retrospective dataset captures unstructured, multi-encounter clinical notes reflecting the real-world complexity of ER patient care.

short_description: ARMD-MGB encompasses data collected from over 200,000 adult patients and over 350,000 microbiological cultures over 10 years from hospitals in the Mass General Brigham healthcare system.
title: Antibiotic Resistance Microbiology Dataset Mass General Brigham (ARMD-MGB)
abstract:
The Antibiotic Resistance Microbiology Dataset – MGB (ARMD-MGB) is a de-identified resource derived from electronic health records (EHR) that facilitates research in antimicrobial resistance (AMR). ARMD-MGB encompasses data collected from over 200,000 adult patients over 10 years from hospitals in the Mass General Brigham healthcare system. The focus of the data is on over 350,000 microbiological cultures, with associated antibiotic susceptibilities, and clinical and demographic features of the patients who submitted the samples. Key attributes include organism identity, antibiotic susceptibility results, implied susceptibility phenotypes, laboratory and vital sign summaries, and de-identified clinical metadata.

The ARMD-MGB dataset is designed to complement the ARMD-Stanford dataset. Cohort inclusion and exclusion criteria, feature descriptions, and encoding are similar across sites. These datasets support studies on antimicrobial stewardship, causal inference, and clinical decision-making, and are designed to be reusable and interoperable, promoting collaboration and innovation in combating AMR.

short_description: Synthetic data for paper "Cuffless hemodynamic monitoring with physics-informed machine learning models".
title: PulseDB-Ext: Blood Pressure and Synthetic Modeled Quantities
abstract: Contained in the database are time-series-split, Fourier truncated blood pressure signals scraped from the PulseDB database along with corresponding modeled time-series of interest. Each entry contains a period length and 100 uniformly spaced values in time. The modeled time-series of interest include the arterial radii, the bulk blood conductivity, and the bioimpedance measured at the wrist. This database is provided to support the development, reproducibility, and benchmarking of physics-informed machine-learning methods for cuffless hemodynamic monitoring.

short_description: The dataset presented was collected during split Timed Up and Down Stairs tests of a novel, robotic ankle foot orthosis (AFO) with adjustable stiffness and manually variable neutral angle for seven individuals with spastic cerebral palsy (CP).
title: Performance Measurements from split Timed Up and Down Stairs test in Cerebral Palsy with and without Ankle Foot Orthoses
abstract: The dataset presented was collected during split Timed Up and Down Stairs tests of a novel, robotic ankle foot orthosis (AFO) with adjustable stiffness and manually variable neutral angle for seven individuals with spastic cerebral palsy (CP). Tests were conducted between May 2025 – October 2025 at Northern Arizona University. Test conditions included nine combinations of stiffness and neutral angle for the robotic AFO, a solid AFO, and shoes alone. Outcomes included TUDs time, peak ankle dorsiflexion and plantarflexion, knee range of motion, soleus and vastus lateralis integrated electromyography, perceived exertion, balance confidence, 3-axis trunk acceleration, and robotic AFO power and torque. These outcomes, conditions, and participant characteristics are reported in this dataset. These data may contribute to 1) further development of robotic ankle foot orthoses and 2) understanding stair ambulation biomechanics in CP.

short_description: MIMIC-IV-Ext-CPT is a credentialed-access benchmark for multi-label CPT/E&M code prediction from deidentified clinical text. It supports reproducible research on long-tailed medical procedure coding using MIMIC-derived clinical reports.
title: MIMIC-IV-Ext-CPT - Procedure Code Labels for MIMIC Clinical Notes
abstract:
MIMIC-IV-Ext-CPT is a credentialed-access dataset for predicting procedure and service code identifiers from deidentified MIMIC clinical notes. Version 1.0.1 contains 30,938 historically curated radiology training records, 7,705 annotated clinical test records, and 412,297 auxiliary records with weak admission-level labels. The auxiliary records come from MIMIC-III radiology and discharge notes and MIMIC-IV-Note discharge summaries.

Each record contains one report and its assigned code set in seven columns: a project-specific sample_id, deidentified report text, pipe-delimited non-E/M cpt_codes, pipe-delimited Evaluation and Management em_codes, and three corresponding label counts. Labels originate from structured coding fields; admission-level labels are not verified evidence of every procedure in an individual note. This revision removes 30 test records whose report text also occurs in training after Unicode, whitespace, and case normalization. Training and auxiliary files are unchanged. Test labels remain within the training vocabulary. The resource supports research on multi-label procedure-code prediction. It does not establish patient-level split independence or support autonomous billing.

short_description: MedVAL-Bench is the first large-scale physician-validated benchmark for medical text validation, spanning 6 diverse medical tasks and containing 840 language model-generated outputs annotated by 12 physicians with error assessments and risk grades.
title: MedVAL-Bench: Expert-Annotated Medical Text Validation Benchmark
abstract: MedVAL-Bench is a dataset containing physician evaluations of errors in language model (LM)-generated medical text. The dataset spans 6 diverse medical text generation tasks and includes annotations from 12 physicians on clinically significant errors for 840 LM-generated outputs. These text-to-text generation tasks involve transforming an input medical text into an output relevant to a specific use case. Each task includes inputs and corresponding LM-generated outputs, which are evaluated for factual consistency by physicians. Importantly, the MedVAL framework and dataset are designed to rely only on inputs for the evaluation process to allow working with datasets that may not have reference outputs, ensuring broad applicability. The evaluation process aims to determine whether the output is factually consistent with the input and is safe for use. MedVAL-Bench constitutes the first large-scale physician-validated benchmark with triage-style risk grading aligned to real-world clinical decision-making, supporting the development of automated, expert-aligned evaluation methods and facilitating research toward trustworthy medical text generation.

short_description: The MIMIC-III-Ext-CA dataset contains annotations of 31 PPG-captured cardiac arrest episodes from the MIMIC-III clinical and waveform databases.
title: MIMIC-III-Ext-CA: a MIMIC-III Derived Dataset of Cardiac Arrests in Photoplethysmographs
abstract: Photoplethysmography (PPG) is increasingly considered for detecting out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but publicly available datasets remain scarce. We used a method for identifying cardiac arrest episodes captured by PPG in the MIMIC-III database, which combines automated screening with manual annotation of waveforms and clinical data. Using this approach, we compiled 36 annotated cardiac arrest episodes from 31 patients. The dataset serves as a valuable resource for developing and validating wearable OHCA detection technologies.

short_description: 720 gastric ultrasound acquisitions from 30 healthy volunteers, imaged in four controlled gastric states in both the supine and right lateral decubitus positions, with protocol-derived state labels.
title: Point-of-Care Gastric Ultrasound in Healthy Volunteers: Cine Loops and Still Images Across Four Controlled Gastric Content States
abstract:
Point-of-care gastric ultrasound is used before anaesthesia to judge whether the stomach is empty, holds clear fluid, or holds solid content, the last being the finding that most changes airway management. Work on automated interpretation has been limited by a lack of openly available data.

This dataset contains 720 gastric ultrasound acquisitions from 30 fasted healthy adult volunteers. Each volunteer was imaged in four gastric states — fasted, after 250 mL of water, early after a solid meal, and late after that meal — in both the supine and right lateral decubitus positions. Each of the eight state-position combinations yielded one still image and two five-second cine loops, giving 240 stills and 480 loops. All imaging was performed by one operator on a single curvilinear system.

Gastric content was set by the study protocol rather than judged from the image, so every acquisition carries a protocol-derived state label. Cine loops are released in full. Every frame is cropped to the acoustic sector, which removes the acquisition date and time, the session code, the manufacturer and hospital logos, the depth scale, and the operator's on-screen annotation. Machine settings and the timing of each acquisition relative to ingestion are provided as tabular files; participant demographics are reported in aggregate only.

A future version will add gastric state labels assigned independently by experienced operators reading the images blind.

short_description: Manual, full-brain segmentations for 10 head computed tomography (CT) examinations from 10 participants in the MISTIE III intracerebral haemorrhage trial.
title: Brain Segmentation Performance in Head CT from MISTIE III Trial
abstract: This resource supports evaluation of automated brain extraction (skull-stripping) in head CT from the MISTIE III intracerebral haemorrhage trial. It has two components. (1) Full-cohort visual QC: for 5,062 scans from 499 participants, PNG overlays (axial, coronal, sagittal) of the brain mask from each of seven methods (CTBET-UNet, 2,403 scans; see Methods), with pass/fail ratings for volumetric, registration and deep-learning failures in CSV files. (2) Manual reference set: for 10 purposively selected examinations from 10 participants, defaced CT volumes, expert full-brain masks, and the masks from the seven automated methods. The 10-scan set was created because other manual datasets used in the accompanying evaluation had been used to train some algorithms. It supports reference-based validation and illustrative benchmarking. It is not for training or for estimating performance in the full MISTIE III population. NIfTI volumes and masks are released for the 10 scans only.

short_description: The Noise Holter Database provides 258 ambulatory ECGs featuring authentic noise and diverse arrhythmias. Segments are expert-annotated into three quality classes to benchmark signal quality assessment algorithms.
title: Noise Holter Database: a multi-device, multi-arrhythmia real-world clinical ECG signal quality benchmark
abstract: The Noise Holter Database is a publicly available, multi-arrhythmia Holter ECG dataset comprising 258 two-lead recordings from distinct subjects. The primary objective of making this resource available is to facilitate the development of software for filtering out noisy segments in ambulatory recordings. The dataset includes a wide spectrum of spontaneous cardiac arrhythmias—including atrial fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia, AV block, and supraventricular tachycardia—captured under real-world ambulatory conditions with authentic environmental noise. Encompassing approximately 35 hours of data, the database features 6,255 ECG segments. These segments include expert-assigned multi-label signal quality annotations classified into three functional levels: Clean (43.7%), N1 where QRS is identifiable (36.0%), and N2 where QRS is unidentifiable (20.3%). Inter-rater agreement, assessed on a comprehensive validation subset of 2,166 events, yielded a Cohen's kappa of 0.83, demonstrating the robustness of the labeling process. This dataset effectively addresses the critical absence of publicly available benchmarks with authentic, naturally occurring ambulatory noise annotations.

short_description: This model is a clinical large language model that effectively captures positivity or negativity (also referred to as clinical sentiment) about patients’ clinical progress in ICU clinical notes.
title: SentimentICUModel: A Clinical Large Language Model for Clinical Sentiment Polarity Identification in ICU Clinical Notes
abstract:
Research has shown that reliance on general-domain lexicons and tools are ineffective in capturing clinical sentiment from ICU clinical notes. However, general-domain methods are prevalent due to difficulty of accessing appropriate clinical data and limited time that specialized clinicians can provide to manually label such data, which is required for models’ development. As a result, clinical sentiment has been under-researched, and no effective model was found for classifying clinical sentiment. This resource addresses this gap by providing an effective model trained for distinguishing clinical sentiment in ICU clinical notes.

This model was trained on clinical notes extracted from MIMIC-III using specific labeling scheme and evaluated vs. clinicians labeling. It enables investigation of clinical sentiment polarity on Intensive Care Unit (ICU) clinical notes, and studying and improving different approaches to sentiment analysis in the clinical text.

The model can be used directly for: (1) further training and evaluating as an independent AI supervised learning model, and (2) developing a hybrid approach incorporating linguistic features or lexicons.

This model was initialized from ClinicalT5 provided in Physionet and trained for clinical sentiment classification. Because ClinicalT5 was trained on MIMIC-III and IV notes, and to avoid the potential leak of data, which can happen with encoder-decoder transformers, ClinicalT5 was only released by Physionet to credentialed users. Therefore, SentimentICUModel is released within Physionet under the same conditions.

short_description: Real intraoperative anaesthetic decisions derived from VitalDB, each with the pre-decision patient state, the action taken and two consensus actions, for evaluating AI systems on choosing the next action.
title: VitalDB - AnesLLM: a dataset and benchmark based on real intraoperative anaesthetic decisions
abstract: AnesLLM is a dataset of real intraoperative anaesthetic decisions derived from VitalDB, an open database of high-resolution recordings from non-cardiac surgery at Seoul National University Hospital. It contains 84 813 decision windows from 3168 anaesthetic cases. Each window is anchored at a decision point and contains only information recorded before it: patient and surgical data, the last preoperative value of 34 laboratory tests, 10 min of vital signs as time series, drug concentrations and ventilatory parameters at the decision point, and a 20-min history of previous actions (280 fields in total). The label is the action actually taken by the anaesthetist, detected automatically from infusion-pump changes: increase or reduce hypnotic, increase or reduce opioid, or no action. Because more than one action is often acceptable, each window also includes the two actions most frequently chosen by the cohort’s anaesthetists in similar clinical states (consensus actions), with their estimated probabilities; vasopressor may appear as an additional, investigator-defined consensus option. Cases are assigned to training (2994), development (25) and test (149) partitions at case level, and the test partition is stratified by case difficulty. The release includes a data dictionary, a partition manifest, a datasheet, machine-readable audit reports (integrity, information leakage, plausibility, drift, missingness and k-anonymity) and command-line utilities to filter windows, convert them to tables or text clinical cases, and verify the integrity of the download. AnesLLM is intended to evaluate any artificial intelligence system on choosing the next action at a specific moment of a real anaesthetic.

short_description: A large-scale corpus of simulated nurse-patient emergency triage dialogues, each grounded in a real MIMIC-IV-ED visit and labelled with its recorded Emergency Severity Index (ESI) level.
title: MIMIC-IV-ED-Ext-TriageSim: A Dataset of Simulated Nurse-Patient Emergency Triage Dialogues Grounded in MIMIC-IV-ED Visits
abstract: Research on emergency department triage is largely restricted to structured electronic health records, because real nurse-patient triage conversations cannot be recorded and shared. We developed TriageSim, a framework that simulates persona-conditioned triage conversations from structured records, and use it with a larger seed set and open-weight models to build MIMIC-IV-ED-Ext-TriageSim: 31,761 simulated English nurse-patient triage dialogues grounded in 4,883 MIMIC-IV-ED visits sampled evenly across the five Emergency Severity Index (ESI) levels, each labelled with the visit's recorded ESI level. We release the training and development sets (22,238 dialogues) of a patient-level 60/10/30 split; the test set is held private. In TriageSim, three language-model agents interact turn by turn: a dialogue master that holds the visit record, enforces consistency with it and keeps the nurse's triage record; a nurse agent that interviews under the ESI algorithm without seeing the recorded level; and a patient agent that answers from what the patient knows about the visit, without vital signs or diagnoses. Nurse and patient personas combine traits documented in emergency care research, such as English proficiency, health literacy, recall, symptom reporting, disclosure, questioning style and workload. Simulations ran locally with three open-weight models (Qwen3.6, Gemma 4 and Nemotron 3 Nano). Patient speech carries filled pauses, repetitions and cut-off words at the persona's disfluency level. Dialogues carry both personas and the nurse's triage record. The corpus supports sequential clinical triage, spoken dialogue modelling, disfluency detection and generation, clinical information extraction, and speech synthesis and recognition research. Audio will follow in a future version.
